The test image shows a soybean field with widespread wilting, browning leaves that remain attached to stems, and some bleached/whitish stems visible throughout. The pattern of wilting across the field in patches, combined with the bleached stem appearance and dead leaves remaining attached, is highly characteristic of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum).

Key distinguishing features:
- Field-level wilting pattern
- Bleached/white stems visible among the canopy
- Dead brown leaves remaining attached to stems
- Plants in reproductive stage showing rapid decline

This matches the White_Mold reference images and symptom description (bleached white dead stems, dead leaves remaining attached, grayish-green wilting).
